title: Real LoRa drivers lack one-shot recv_async contract (lr1110/sim/renode -ENOTSUP, 3-arg stubs vs v3.7.0 2-arg pin)
description: Found by 3x codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-sb0b (correctness/security/robustness). The async L2 RX (sb0b) requires a one-shot recv_async: driver delivers one packet, disarms, L2 re-arms after processing. Current state: (1) lichen/drivers/lora/lr1110/lr1110.c:627, lora_sim.c:433, lora_renode.c:279 are -ENOTSUP stubs AND use the 3-arg (dev,cb,user_data) signature, which is incompatible with the pinned Zephyr v3.7.0 2-arg lora_recv_async(dev,cb) - any config building those drivers cannot compile under the pin, while 4.1.0-workspace builds break the new 2-arg L2 call sites instead. (2) With fail-closed start() (sb0b), lichen_lora_l2_start() on T1000-E (LR1110, primary bench target) always reverts to STOPPED until the driver implements recv_async. Fix: implement 2-arg one-shot recv_async in lr1110/lora_sim/lora_renode (DIO1 RX_DONE IRQ -> cb -> disarm; NULL cb cancels), or gate those boards explicitly at build time. Loopback driver in sb0b is the reference implementation.
